# Attachment Access Functions

A reusable compute definition extending Activation Functions to register attachment access publications and install a designated authority party. It also inherits activation, party management, access validation, admission, mapping and amendment helpers. Functions act when invoked; this definition alone does not establish a viewer’s permission or obligation.

Paths refer to the document in which the functions execute. `call/channel` identifies the invoking channel; `call/requireExactDocumentVersion` carries the exact-review requirement. The execution constants `key` and `authority` select the attachment namespace and authority party key; their values and defaults are not supplied here.

## Registering attachment access

`registerAccessPublic(input)` delegates to `registerAccess`. `input.documents` must contain one to sixteen existing Timeline Access publications. Each must have a Public Timeline Channel at `/contracts/provider`, an initialization document at `/contracts/initialized/document`, and provider history at `/contracts/checkpoint/entries/provider`.

Registration requires `call/requireExactDocumentVersion` to equal `true`, `call/channel` to be a key in `/activation/parties`, parties to be unfrozen, and `/activation/allowNewParties` to permit additions. These guards reject with `ATTACHMENT_EXACT_REVIEW_REQUIRED`, `ONLY_PARTY_LEAD_CAN_MANAGE`, `PARTIES_FROZEN` or `NEW_PARTIES_DISABLED`. For these checks, absent `frozen` and `allowNewParties` are treated as `false`. Missing `documents` becomes an empty list and is rejected.

New registration stores publication references at `/attachmentAccess_<key>/<index>`, using zero-based indices, and appends those paths to `/activation/accessPaths`. It installs each publication’s provider channel as `attachmentAccess_<key>_<index>` under `/contracts`, with a corresponding `_refresh` workflow that invokes Refresh Activation. It returns `outcome: acceptedNew`; registration itself does not call `refresh`.

An existing namespace returns `outcome: duplicate` only when its size and every publication identity at the corresponding index match. Different publications, ordering or count reject with `ATTACHMENT_ACCESS_ALREADY_REGISTERED`. The caller and document guards still apply to duplicate requests.

Registration records access evidence and refresh wiring; it does not change `allowedKeys` or `allowedTimelines`, or itself establish participant access readiness. Unlike inherited `validateAccessDocument`, this registration path does not compare the publication’s original and current executable policies against the native policy.

## Installing the authority party

`addAuthority(input)` requires exact review, an unfrozen roster and a party-lead channel. If the party selected by constant `authority` already exists, only that party’s lead channel may replace it; otherwise the call rejects with `CANNOT_MANAGE_ANOTHER_PARTY`.

It delegates to `installAuthority`, which forces `input.party` to the `authority` constant. `input.replacement` supplies the complete replacement party and must include `lead.channel`. Optional `representatives` are keyed by representative names. Party and representative keys must be nonempty text without `.`, `/`, `~` or `__`. Adding a previously absent authority requires `allowNewParties`; replacing an existing authority does not.

The resulting roster must pass `accessValid`. Generated roster contracts must not collide with existing contracts outside the previous roster’s contributions. Success installs channels and approval/update handlers, replaces the target party, clears all `approved` entries, adds a newly introduced party to `required`, and increments `revision` by one, using 1 when the previous revision is absent. It writes the result of `computeState` to `/activation`, emits Party Changed with `party` and `revision`, and returns `true`.

`installAuthority` performs installation checks but does not repeat `addAuthority`’s exact-review or caller checks. It uses `computeState` directly, so it does not perform `commitState`’s terms-reference updates, channel reconciliation or activation-transition events.

## Access and activation meaning

`accessValid` checks every lead and additional representative transport. External Channel transports require no Timeline Access match in this check. Other transports must be Timeline Channels. Each such timeline needs at least one access document listed in `accessPaths` whose timeline and provider match and whose `allowedKeys` contain at least one key from every reader group. All groups must be covered by the same matching document for that transport.

`readerGroups` combines configured `readers` with party `readerKeys` under the party key and representative `readerKeys` under `<party>__<representative>`. Roster entries override matching configured group names. Missing reader-key lists become empty groups, which cannot satisfy a key match. Reading access and authority to operate remain separate.

`computeState` derives `/activation` fields:

- `accessReady` and `functional` report access validity, including proposed parties in `accessRequests` whose `expectedRevision` matches the current revision.
- `termsAccepted` requires approval of every role in `required` and agreement between current document values and `/activation/terms/fields`.
- `active` additionally requires access readiness and an unclosed document.
- `status` is `CLOSED` when closed; otherwise `WAITING_FOR_ACCESS` or `SUSPENDED_ACCESS` when access is missing, distinguished by `everActivated`; otherwise `AWAITING_ACCEPTANCE` or `ACTIVE`.
- `reason` prioritizes `PARTICIPANT_ACCESS_MISSING`, then `ACCEPTANCE_REQUIRED`, otherwise an empty string. It is not a separate closure explanation.

Within these computations, missing collections use empty collections and missing approval, closure and activation-history flags use `false`. These are execution fallbacks, not evidence that an absent stored result is false or complete.

## Inherited activation operations

`approve` requires exact review, a party-lead channel, `input.revision` matching `/activation/revision`, and valid participant access. When `/clauses/activation/parameters/negotiation/allowedPaths` is nonempty, a text `termsRef` is required; any supplied reference must match `/activation/terms/ref`. `approveWithTerms` delegates to this operation. A previously approved party returns `true` after validation. A new approval is committed and emits Terms Accepted. Approval alone does not imply activation: all activation conditions must hold. When the commit reports active, negotiation becomes uneditable and any pending proposal is marked `SUPERSEDED` and cleared.

`updatePartyPublic` delegates to `updateParty`. Its optional `party` defaults to the invoking channel; `replacement.lead.channel` is required and no input revision is required. It applies the same exact-review, roster, naming, access and contract-conflict protections described above: existing parties can only replace themselves, while additions require `allowNewParties`. It clears approvals and increments the activation revision, but uses `commitState` rather than the authority installer’s direct computation.

`refresh` initializes terms when absent, commits derived activation state and refreshes admission-access readiness. `initializeTerms` captures allowed scalar negotiation fields and a definition identity excluding access evidence, configured readers and party reader keys; it starts `termsRevision` and negotiation `revision` at 1. `commitState` updates terms identity when parties or required approvers change, clears pending proposals with `AUTHORITY_CHANGED`, and clears approvals when negotiation paths are configured. Initial transports remain empty composite channels until access is ready. Commits track `everActivated` and emit Document Activated, Document Access Suspended or Document Access Restored on their defined transitions.

`requestPartyAddition` consumes event data, ignores stale revisions and previously recorded `admissionRef` values, validates supplied party access publications, and records requests where existing parties’ timelines lack coverage for the proposed reader groups. Party Access Update Requested is a request, not permission evidence or confirmation that access changed. `refreshAccessRequests` updates readiness for requests at the current revision. `admitApprovedParties` requires an unfrozen roster, matching `expectedRevision`, nonempty configured `admission.approvers`, compatible main identities and valid access. An unchanged roster returns `duplicate`; otherwise it installs contracts, increments revision, commits and emits Party Changed with admission details. The helper itself does not collect approver votes.

Inherited `installTimelineAccess` accepts one to sixteen publications, validates native executable policy, deduplicates by initialization identity and installs embedded update-event refresh channels. `requirePartyAccessDocuments` checks supplied role coverage, reader-key presence and timeline/provider correspondence. Permission changes remain provider-owned.

Inherited party mapping resolves declared roles to compatible main identities without granting access or consent. Amendment helpers record proposals against an expected revision and permitted editable path; configured approvers must all approve before replacement is applied. Recording or approving a proposal is distinct from its completed application.

Provider permission enforcement beyond the supplied definitions is not established here; registration or an emitted request alone does not confirm an external access outcome.
